item.text:
Completed the continuation research for all selected chapters: 2B, 3B, 6B, and 7B. No scores or ranking judgments were produced.

The workspace was read-only, so I could not persist `research-materials.md` or `research-ledger-manifest.json`. Below is the persistence-ready research delta.

### 2B — International peace, restraint, and lawful security

New defensible units:

- Germany’s official Ukraine-arms process required Defense Ministry review, Chancellor’s Office, Foreign Office, and Economy Ministry input; end-use clauses restricted onward transfer without German consent. Attribution is governmental, not solely Scholz. [Federal Government arms FAQ](https://www.bundesregierung.de/breg-de/service/fragen-und-anworten/faq-waffenlieferungen-2027766), sections “How are weapons deliveries decided?” and “What does the end-use clause mean?”
- The Bundestag recorded the government’s claim that it had no evidence of German-supplied weapons being used in Gaza and that licenses would be denied where a clear risk of serious IHL violations existed. This is an official claim, not independent verification. [Bundestag Israel-export report](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-1009274), opening paragraphs.
- A December 2023 European Parliament question documented continuing concern that EU arms exports to Israel could breach IHL and cited the legal duty to deny licenses where a clear risk existed. This is contrary procedural evidence, not proof of German illegality. [European Parliament question P-003630/2023](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/P-9-2023-003630_EN.html).
- Bundestag debate records preserved contrary views on Scholz’s Taurus restraint: supporters described it as necessary prudence, while coalition and opposition critics said delay could itself increase escalation risk. [Bundestag Ukraine debate](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2023/kw46-de-ukraine-976574), paragraphs around the Taurus debate.

Remaining gaps: item-level end-use monitoring, individual licensing records, humanitarian-law diligence, and a reliable counterfactual assessment of Taurus restraint.

### 3B — Domestic safety, restraint, and protection

New defensible/context units:

- Official 2023 figures recorded 256,276 victims of domestic violence, with roughly 70% female; the responsible ministry presented a federal assistance-system law as the intended remedy. This establishes a target-year protection burden, not Scholz causation. [BMFSFJ domestic-violence release](https://www.bmfsfj.de/bmfsfj/aktuelles/presse/pressemitteilungen/haeusliche-gewalt-im-jahr-2023-um-6-5-prozent-gestiegen-241062), headline and lead.
- Amnesty’s November 2023 UPR submission identified racial discrimination, hate crimes, gender-based violence, assembly restrictions, and the lack of independent police-complaint mechanisms. [Amnesty Germany UPR submission](https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/eur23/6481/2023/en/), summary.
- The Federal Anti-Discrimination Agency’s 2023 report said the proposed Federal Police Act did not adequately prohibit racial profiling and could permit arbitrary “objective reasons” for identity checks. [Anti-Discrimination Agency annual report](https://www.antidiskriminierungsstelle.de/EN/homepage/_documents/annual_report_2023_englisch.pdf), pp. 15–17.
- The Federal Constitutional Court held that routine handcuffing during prisoner medical transfers without individualized assessment raised constitutional and ECHR proportionality concerns. This demonstrates judicial remedy and an institutional detention problem, not a Scholz-specific decision. [Federal Constitutional Court order](https://www.bundesverfassungsgericht.de/SharedDocs/Entscheidungen/EN/2023/01/rk20230119_2bvr171921en.html).
- Destatis released 2023 prison statistics based on the 31 March 2023 prison population, confirming an accessible official source for detention demographics, though the spreadsheet was not extracted in this pass. [Destatis prison statistics](https://www.destatis.de/DE/Themen/Staat/Justiz-Rechtspflege/Publikationen/Downloads-Strafverfolgung-Strafvollzug/statistischer-bericht-strafvollzug-2100410237005.html).

Remaining gaps: prison conditions beyond the cited judicial remedy, federal control over Länder policing, shelter-capacity implementation, and measurable year-over-year safety change.

### 6B — Social well-being and human development

New defensible/context units:

- The OECD’s 2023 Germany health profile explicitly covered health status, access, effectiveness, resilience, and mental-health services. The accessible HTML did not expose the report’s detailed outcome tables, so this is report-scope evidence rather than a health-outcome claim. [OECD Germany Country Health Profile 2023](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/germany-country-health-profile-2023_21dd4679-en.html), publication metadata and abstract.
- The Bundestag reported €42.6 billion in 2023 Bürgergeld payment entitlements, broken down by household type. This establishes scale and administrative reach, not adequacy or impact. [Bundestag Bürgergeld expenditure report](https://www.bundestag.de/presse/hib/kurzmeldungen-1013412), opening paragraph.
- Destatis reported €17.6 billion in SGB XII social-assistance spending, up 18%, and €25.4 billion in disability-integration assistance spending, up 9.4%. Bürgergeld was explicitly excluded from these figures. [Destatis social-assistance statistics](https://www.destatis.de/DE/Presse/Pressemitteilungen/2024/08/PD24_295_221.html), paragraphs 1–4.
- Destatis reported that 23.9% of German children under 18 were at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2023, while the income-based child-poverty rate was 14.0%. [Destatis child-poverty release](https://www.destatis.de/DE/Presse/Pressemitteilungen/2024/07/PD24_N033_63.html), paragraphs on 2023 results.
- BAMF’s 2023 integration-course statistics page confirms a national 2023 administrative dataset, while its evaluation project identifies access, course effectiveness, and refugee outcomes as research questions. [BAMF 2023 integration-course statistics](https://www.bamf.de/SharedDocs/Anlagen/DE/Statistik/Integrationskurszahlen/Bundesweit/2023-integrationskursgeschaeftsstatistik-gesamt_bund.html), and [BAMF integration-course evaluation](https://www.bamf.de/SharedDocs/ProjekteReportagen/DE/Forschung/Integration/evaluation-integrationskurse.html).

The health-profile gateway remains discovery-only for detailed outcome extraction. Social-service outcomes, education, disability access, migrant-service quality, and Bürgergeld effects remain substantially lagged or unavailable for 2023.

### 7B — Personal integrity and honesty

New defensible/context units:

- Germany’s Whistleblower Protection Act entered into force on 2 July 2023, prohibiting retaliation, requiring secure reporting channels, and protecting work-related disclosures. This is a coalition institutional-integrity reform, not evidence of Scholz’s personal conduct. [Library of Congress legal monitor](https://www.loc.gov/item/global-legal-monitor/2023-07-13/germany-whistleblower-protection-act-enters-into-force/), paragraphs 1–8.
- The Bundestag record shows the government’s proposal for internal and external reporting offices, confidentiality protections, and compensation for retaliation. [Bundestag whistleblower debate](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2023/kw19_de_schutz_hinweisgebender_personen-946698), sections on reporting offices and retaliation.
- A Bundestag transparency hearing identified unresolved lobbying gaps, including the absence of an independent review body and a legislative “footprint” showing concrete influence on laws and regulations. [Bundestag Lobby Register hearing](https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2023/kw42-de-lobbyregister-971428), paragraphs 764–830 and 916.
- Contrary evidence remains concentrated in Cum-Ex: parliamentary and prosecutorial records document continuing dispute over Scholz’s memory accounts, inquiry refusal, and legal status, while no legally established personal misconduct was recovered.

The chapter remains dominated by one contested scandal. No reliable 2023 evidence was found on Scholz’s assets, gifts, procurement conflicts, appointments, personal enrichment, or treatment of whistleblowers.
